question: Apple has announced that certain Siri AI features will not be made available to iPhone and iPad users in the EU, citing the interoperability requirements of the Digital Markets Act (DMA). The Commission has stated that nothing in the DMA prevents Apple from introducing these services in the EU and that it remains in discussions with Apple on a safe and DMAcompliant solution.
It has also stated that Apple has not yet presented a concrete interoperability proposal beyond requesting an exemption from the relevant requirements for more than 18 months. In this context: 1.

What engagement has taken place between the Commission and Apple since the announcement of the delayed EU rollout of Siri AI, and has Apple subsequently presented any concrete technical proposal for DMA-compliant interoperability?

Does the Commission consider that a solution can be found which enables the timely rollout of Siri AI in the EU while ensuring both effective interoperability and appropriate safeguards for users’ privacy and security?
What further steps does the Commission envisage to facilitate such a solution and avoid EU consumers facing a prolonged delay in accessing these services?
